title: Variance-controlled rollout orchestrator with adaptive step sizing and safety probes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a policy engine and config surface that performs canary rollouts using adaptive step sizes driven by observed metric variance and cohort-specific probes. The engine will compute safe next-step traffic allocations (including fractional percentages), enforce hard guardrails (latency, error, hallucination), run shadow probes in parallel, and trigger automated rollback or hold actions when thresholds are breached. This is intended to reduce time-to-safe-rollout for model updates while minimizing user impact and unnecessary rollbacks.
motivation: Current manual canary workflows are conservative and require frequent human intervention. Static step schedules either progress too slowly (wasting capacity and delaying improvements) or too quickly (increasing blast-radius). Using observed variance for key metrics enables principled step sizing that adapts to signal quality and magnitude, improving safety and speed.
design_notes: Core idea: policy expression DSL + runtime evaluator. DSL supports schedule blocks (initial, adaptive, steady), metric guards (p50_latency < 120ms, p95_latency < 350ms, error_rate_delta < 0.5%), and variance rules (use SE/CI on metric to compute minimum safe increment). The runtime will: 1) sample live telemetry for the canary cohort, 2) compute metric variance and confidence intervals, 3) pick next_step = min(max_step, floor( z_alpha * se_ratio * base_step )), 4) validate against hard guardrails, 5) apply traffic split via routing layer and start shadow probes. See example config snippet: "{\"type\":\"adaptive\",\"initial\":5,\"max_step\":25,\"alpha\":0.95,\"metrics\":[{\"name\":\"p95_latency\",\"guard\":{\"op\":\"<\",\"value\":350}},{\"name\":\"error_rate\",\"guard\":{\"op\":\"<\",\"value\":0.005}}]}". Implementation will require changes to Router API, rollout controller, and telemetry query layer.
tasks: Spec review and finalize DSL (PM + SRE + Runtime)
Implement DSL parser and validation (runtime module)
Extend rollout controller to compute adaptive step using telemetry API
Add shadow probe orchestration and sampling hooks
Create simulation harness to replay historical telemetry for validation
End-to-end tests and integrate with Console rollout UI
Docs: config reference and runbook for on-call
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive rollout config accepted by runtime and validated by unit tests
Simulation harness shows at least 20% faster median time-to-safe-rollout across a set of historical updates while maintaining <1% increase in rollback rate
Automated rollback triggers when any hard guardrail is violated for configured evaluation window
Rollout controller emits audit logs for every traffic change and decision reason visible in Console
Integration test covering a staged rollout with shadow probes and a forced fault injection that causes rollback
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff sync with PM and SRE. Agreed on initial metric set: p50, p95, error_rate, hallucination_rate (from eval harness).
2026-02-18: Draft DSL merged to Google doc. Trade-off: simpler DSL wins for first iteration; advanced Bayesian module deferred to follow-up.
2026-02-24: Router API stubbed; need routing contract change to accept fractional traffic with annotation for audit reasons.

2026-03-01: Simulation harness ingest pipeline built; replayed three historical model flips. Adaptive algorithm picked smaller steps for high-variance cohorts and passed guardrails in two of three cases.
2026-03-05: Prototype for step computation landed (internal PR). Metrics team requested slight change to SE estimator; follow-up assigned.
notes_on_decisions: Chose frequentist CI approach for first rollout because it's easier to explain to on-call and integrates into existing telemetry queries. Bayesian stopping considered but deferred due to compute and explainability concerns. Will evaluate Bayesian module in follow-up EPIC.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy hallucination metric may cause premature holds. Mitigation: require a minimum sample size and add cohort-level smoothing and shadow-probe amplification. Risk: fractional traffic rounding in router could bias splits. Mitigation: router will use traffic tokenization and short-lived sticky routing to approximate fractional flows.
review_feedback: PM (Elena Wu): emphasize Console UX for manual override and rationale display
SRE (Marco Diaz): require explicit error-budget delta guard and integration with incident alerting
Design (Priya Nair): request a compact visual for predicted next-step probability and confidence to show in rollout detail view
follow_up_todos: Metrics: surface hallucination_rate in p95 dashboards (ENG-205011)
